correctness.rationale: Walsh singleton and pair test functions give valid spectral-gap upper bounds 2(b+a) and 4b for every independently weighted edge allocation, with means b=2B/(dN), a=2A/N. Uniform edge classes diagonalize exactly in Walsh basis with eigenvalues 2kb+2a when k odd; the gap equals min(2(b+a),4b) for all d>=4. Linear budget N(db+ta)/2=1 produces the displayed sharp t=d threshold and segment. Equality in average Rayleigh inequalities forces each singleton/pair Walsh character to be an actual lowest eigenvector; pointwise equations force all coordinate and antipodal weights uniform even at the transition, ruling out irregular optima. Independent explicit full-Laplacian eigenspectra corroborate for d=4,5 and prices across the threshold.
